Modulate

/MOJ-uh-layt/ - the stress falls on MOJ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Modulate means to shift or adjust gradually from one level or tone to another.

Descending the gravel switchbacks, she modulated the brakes constantly, feathering them lighter and firmer so the wheels never quite locked.

Worked Example

Good hosts modulate a dinner party without anyone noticing: the music eases lower as plates arrive, the lamps warm by a shade, and the conversation is steered gently from politics toward dessert.

Modulate is control, not drift: whoever modulates a thing moves it deliberately and by degrees. A voice that cracks has changed; a voice that sinks smoothly to a hush has been modulated. Where fluctuate reports unplanned movement, modulate claims a steady hand.

How Modulate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

adjust

adjust: the everyday word for small corrections, made one at a time

regulate

regulate: to hold something at a set level by rule or mechanism

fine-tune

fine-tune: to make tiny final corrections once the level is already close

Antonyms

jolt

jolt: to move something in one sudden jerk

blare

blare: to hold at full, unvarying loudness

How Strong Is It? — tweak → adjust → modulate

tweak vs. modulate

tweak vs. modulate: A tweak is milder than modulating — one tiny one-off correction, while modulating shapes the whole curve of a change.

adjust vs. modulate

adjust vs. modulate: Adjust is milder than modulate — an adjustment fixes a setting once and steps away, while modulating keeps a hand on the dial the whole time.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — modul-

Root — modul-: a small measure (Latin modulus, from modus, 'measure')

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make or do

Put it together

Put it together: Modul- (a small measure, from Latin modulus, the diminutive of modus, 'measure') + -ate (to do) = to work in small measures. Latin modulari meant to keep time in music — to portion sound into measures — and modulate still means changing something the way a musician does: by controlled, measured degrees.

Use the root in a new word: modify

Use the root in a new word: modify: Engineers modified the wing after testing, lengthening it by a hand's width.

Word Choice

formal / technical

Modulate suits voices, signals, doses, and light — anything eased between levels by a controlling hand. If the change is one plain correction, adjust is enough; if a device holds a level automatically, regulate; keep modulate for smooth, deliberate shading, the opposite of this unit's jumpy fluctuate.
